# Dormeto savings estimate

Account 111122223333, estimated 2026-11-14 10:00 UTC from the last 14 days of requests (2026-10-31 10:00 to 2026-11-14 10:00 UTC).

> not in an organization: only the account 111122223333 is estimated

## Totals

Dormeto would save about **$104.16 a month** at each workload's recommended idle window (standalone resources: a 2-hour idle window), for 1 workload and 2 standalone resources. Dormeto itself costs about $5.65 a month: **net about $98.51**.

## Options

- Accounts: every account reached
- Regions: each account's enabled regions
- EC2 uptime: 24/7 assumed (--ec2-uptime measures it)
- ECS uptime: at the desired count when discovered, all the time (--ecs-uptime measures it)
- RDS uptime: companion databases available all the time assumed, one stopped left out (--rds-uptime measures it)
- Excluded tags: none
- Role in member accounts: OrganizationAccountAccessRole
- Baseline: 24/7
- Discounts: compute 0%, databases 0%
- Requests: the last 14 days (--days)
- Idle window of the figures: each workload's recommended window (--window sets one for every workload)
- Wakes a day: at most 3 at each workload's recommended window, the busier left out (--max-wakes)
- Minimum saving: $1.00 a month at each workload's recommended window, the smaller left out (--min-saving)
- Companion databases: found by security group, left out when their workload wakes more than 2 times a day at its recommended window (--max-wakes-rds)
- Standalone resources: estimated (--standalone on), at a 2-hour idle window (--standalone-window), idle by their default signals

## Assumptions

- Every request counts as activity and as a wake: no waker is installed yet to set scanners and other filtered requests apart, so the workloads stay awake longer here than they would (smaller savings).
- A wake lasts 60 seconds in the replay; the visitors' wait is not estimated before install.
- Prices: AWS's on-demand list prices, Spot prices for Spot capacity, less the discounts given (compute 0%, databases 0%); storage, load balancers and data transfer are not counted.
- Savings counted within every hour (24/7).
- EC2 instances without an Auto Scaling group are assumed to run 24/7 (--ec2-uptime measures it): one stopped at night by a schedule saves less than estimated here.
- ECS services are assumed to run all the time at their desired count when discovered (--ecs-uptime measures when they had a task): one scaled to 0 at night by a schedule saves less than estimated here.
- Companion databases are found by security group (a database whose security group lets a workload's in), RDS instances and Aurora provisioned clusters, not yet Aurora Serverless; one another workload reaches, a read replica or one with replicas is left out; with --rds-uptime their CPUUtilization says when they were available (one stopped when discovered, started by a schedule, included), else they are assumed available all the time and one stopped is left out; their storage keeps billing, and a database takes minutes to start (its workload's wakes are held that long, not counted here).
- Dormeto's cost: about $5 a month for the manager, $0.26 per account and region with workloads, $0.13 per workload.
